# Sirach Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_010_page_001.jpg

---

1 A wise judge educates his people, and good government depends on the understanding of its leaders.

2 As the ruler of a people is, so are his officials; as the head of a city is, so are all its inhabitants.

3 An undisciplined king brings ruin to his people, but a city flourishes through the wisdom of its rulers.

4 Sovereignty over the earth belongs to the Lord, and at the right moment he will raise up over it the right person.

5 Human success is in the hand of the Lord; it is he who confers dignity on the one who makes the law.

6 Do not be resentful of your neighbor for any wrong done, and do not act arrogantly in anything you do.

7 Arrogance is hateful before the Lord and before people, and injustice is offensive to both.

8 Sovereignty passes from nation to nation because of violence, arrogance, and greed.

9 Why should dust and ashes be arrogant? For even now in life the body is decaying.

10 A slight illness mocks the physician; even a king may be alive today and dead tomorrow.

11 For when a person dies, he becomes the inheritance of maggots, wild beasts, and worms.

12 The beginning of human pride is to forsake the Lord; the heart has turned away from its Maker.

13 For pride is the source of sin, and those who harbor it bring forth abomination; for that reason the Lord sends calamities on them and reduces them to ruin.

14 The Lord has toppled the thrones of rulers, and set the lowly in their place.

15 The Lord has uprooted the proud nations, and planted the humble in their place.

16 The Lord has laid waste the lands of the nations and destroyed them to their very foundations.

17 He has swept some of them away and destroyed them, and has blotted out all memory of them from the earth.

18 Pride was not ordained for human beings, nor violent anger for those born of women.

19 Whose descendants deserve honor? Those who fear the Lord. Whose descendants deserve dishonor? Those who violate his commandments.

20 Among one's own people, a leader is worthy of honor; those who fear the Lord are worthy of honor in his sight.

21 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of favor with him; obstinacy and arrogance mark the beginning of rejection.

22 Whether rich, renowned, or poor — their glory is the fear of the Lord.

23 It is wrong to despise a poor person who is intelligent, and it is wrong to honor a sinful person.

24 The great, the judge, and the ruler are all worthy of honor, but none is greater than the one who fears the Lord.

25 Free citizens will serve an intelligent servant, and a person of understanding will accept it without complaint.

26 Do not make a display of your wisdom in your work, and do not show off your cleverness at an unsuitable time.

27 A laborer who has plenty of everything is better off than someone who goes around making an impression but lacks bread.

28 My child, hold yourself in esteem with humility, and value yourself at your true worth.

29 Who can acquit a person who sins against himself? Who can honor a person who brings dishonor on himself?

30 A poor person is honored for his knowledge, and a rich person is honored for his wealth.

31 One honored in poverty — how much more when wealthy! And one dishonored in wealth — how much more when poor!
